## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest)

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format that makes tutorials versioned
and testable independently of Dashboard releases: the metadata a packaged
tutorial carries, the pinned workbench images it references, and the validation
manifest used to test it against a release. The format is the contract between
the tutorial gallery (which launches packaged tutorials) and tutorial authors
(who produce them), so it is defined before either the gallery or the tutorials
are built.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial package format covering, per the strategy: metadata,
  pinned images, and a validation manifest.
- Specify how a package is versioned so tutorials can be updated and tested on
  their own cadence, decoupled from Dashboard releases.
- Specify how the validation manifest is used to test a tutorial against a
  given release (the mechanism the curated tutorial set is tested with).
- Cover both tutorial kinds the gallery launches: a notebook launched into a
  workbench, and a pipeline imported into a project.
- Keep the format a contract only — the gallery implementation and the tutorial
  content are separate work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format is documented and covers metadata, pinned images, and a
  validation manifest for both notebook-based and pipeline-based tutorials.
- A tutorial package can be versioned, and its version is distinguishable from
  the Dashboard release it is tested against.
- Given a packaged tutorial and a target release, the validation manifest
  defines a runnable pass/fail test of the tutorial against that release, and
  this is demonstrated on at least one sample package of each kind (notebook
  and pipeline).
- The format is reviewed with the teams that consume it (the Dashboard gallery
  implementers and the tutorial authors) and their feedback is incorporated.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1) — "A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases." This epic fully covers HLR-3. Epic
  priority is P0 by inheritance: every P0 deliverable of the strategy (the
  gallery and the curated tutorials) builds against this format.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch into a project

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated, visible
gallery of getting-started tutorials from which a user can launch a tutorial
into their own project with one click — opening a workbench preloaded with the
tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline into the project. This is
the product-code work stream of the strategy, owned by the Dashboard team.

## Scope

- Add a tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard (listing curated tutorials
  with their metadata from the tutorial packaging format).
- Implement one-click launch into the user's project:
  - For notebook tutorials: spawn a workbench with the tutorial notebook,
    using the pinned image from the tutorial package.
  - For pipeline tutorials: import the pipeline into the user's project.
- Launch mechanics operate through the existing Kubernetes CR surfaces the
  Dashboard already reads and writes (Notebook CRs, pipeline resources).
- Gallery visibility/enablement follows the Dashboard's existing per-component
  feature flag mechanism.
- Incidental UI text and screenshot updates that fall out of this change are
  included here; no new documentation topics are authored in this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user with a project, when they open the tutorial gallery and click a
  notebook tutorial, then a workbench opens in their project running the
  tutorial notebook on the pinned image.
- Given a user with a project, when they click a pipeline tutorial, then the
  tutorial pipeline is imported into their project.
- The gallery renders the curated tutorial set from packages conforming to the
  tutorial packaging format, with no tutorial content hardcoded in the
  Dashboard.
- The gallery is verified against at least one packaged notebook tutorial and
  one packaged pipeline tutorial.
- The feature can be enabled/disabled through the Dashboard's existing
  configuration mechanism.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0) — "The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook,
  or importing the pipeline)." This epic fully covers HLR-1.

# Five notebook-based getting-started tutorials (workbench, data prep, training, deployment, RAG)

## Description

This epic authors the five notebook-based tutorials of the curated
getting-started set, covering the core journeys that run in a workbench: first
workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and first RAG app.
Each tutorial is authored as content, packaged per the tutorial packaging
format, and tested against the current release. This is substantive content
authoring — a distinct work stream from the gallery product code.

## Scope

- Author five curated notebook tutorials:
  1. First workbench — creating and using a first workbench.
  2. Data prep — preparing data in a workbench.
  3. First training run — training a first model.
  4. First deployment — deploying a first model from a workbench.
  5. First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented-generation app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  workbench images, validation manifest) so it is versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases.
- Test each tutorial against the current release using its validation
  manifest, and fix content that fails.
- Curate the content for a new-user audience (time-to-first-success is the
  strategy's driver); keep tutorials maintained as part of the curated set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist covering first workbench, data prep, first
  training run, first deployment, and first RAG app.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format with metadata,
  a pinned workbench image, and a validation manifest.
- Each tutorial's validation run passes against the current release (pass/fail
  per tutorial, evidenced by the validation manifest results).
- Each tutorial is launchable from the Dashboard tutorial gallery into a user
  project (verified as part of the tutorial's validation).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, partial) — "Six curated tutorials exist covering the core
  journeys … Each is tested against the current release." This epic covers the
  five notebook-based journeys; the first-pipeline tutorial is a separate epic
  under the Data Science Pipelines component and team.

# First-pipeline getting-started tutorial (KFP pipeline)

## Description

This epic authors the first-pipeline tutorial of the curated getting-started
set: a maintained, tested tutorial that walks a new user through building and
running their first data science pipeline. The tutorial is a pipeline artifact
(imported into the user's project by the gallery's launch mechanics), authored
and owned by the pipelines team, packaged per the tutorial packaging format,
and tested against the current release.

## Scope

- Author the first-pipeline tutorial covering the core "first pipeline"
  journey (creating and running a first pipeline in a project), as a pipeline
  artifact a user can launch from the tutorial gallery.
- Package the tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest) so it is versioned and testable independently
  of Dashboard releases.
- Test the tutorial against the current release using its validation
  manifest, and fix content that fails.
- Curate the content for a new-user audience consistent with the rest of the
  getting-started set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The first-pipeline tutorial exists and covers the first-pipeline core
  journey.
- The tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format with metadata,
  pinned images, and a validation manifest.
- The tutorial's validation run passes against the current release (evidenced
  by the validation manifest results).
- The tutorial is importable from the Dashboard tutorial gallery into a user
  project (verified as part of the tutorial's validation).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, partial) — "Six curated tutorials exist covering the core
  journeys … Each is tested against the current release." This epic covers the
  first-pipeline journey; the five notebook-based journeys are a separate epic
  under the Notebooks component and Workbenches team.

# Documentation for gallery usage and tutorial contribution process

## Description

This epic documents the tutorial gallery for users and contributors: how to
use the gallery to launch tutorials into a project, and how to contribute new
tutorials to the curated set (the contribution process only — no submission
tooling this release, per the strategy's out-of-scope statement). It is the
documentation work stream of the strategy and runs after the implementations
so the docs describe what was actually built.

## Scope

- Author documentation covering using the tutorial gallery:
  - What the gallery is and where to find it in the Dashboard.
  - How to launch a notebook tutorial into a workbench and a pipeline tutorial
    into a project.
- Author documentation covering the contribution process for new tutorials:
  - The tutorial packaging format an author must conform to (metadata, pinned
    images, validation manifest).
  - How a contributed tutorial is versioned, tested against a release, and
    reviewed for inclusion in the curated set.
- Content outline:
  1. Using the tutorial gallery (user guide topic).
  2. Contributing a new tutorial (contributor guide topic).
- Incidental references in existing docs that fall out of the gallery change
  are updated as part of the relevant topics; no other doc topics are
  rewritten.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the tutorial gallery, including
  launching both a notebook tutorial and a pipeline tutorial.
- Published documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials,
  including the packaging format and validation requirements a contribution
  must meet.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery
  and the shipped tutorial set, and any inaccuracies found in review are
  fixed.
- The documentation makes clear that community/partner submission tooling and
  content localization are out of scope for this release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2) — "Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials." This epic fully covers HLR-4. Epic priority is
  P1, derived from the strategy's frontmatter priority (Major → P1) per the
  docs-authoring priority exception.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019: Curated getting-started tutorial gallery

multiple architecturally distinct work streams with different owners and review

content authoring (six curated, tested tutorials), and documentation — so the
below-threshold escape condition for multiple distinct work streams applies and
full decomposition proceeds.

| E001 → E003 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | Authored tutorials are delivered as packages conforming to the format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) so they are versioned and testable; the packaging format must exist before the tutorial deliverables are produced against it. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | Same as above — the pipeline tutorial is delivered as a package conforming to the format. |
| E001 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | docs-authoring epic is blocked by ALL Implementation epics in the strategy. |
| E002 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation describes what was built, including the gallery. |
| E003 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation covers the tutorial set and contribution process. |
| E004 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation covers the tutorial set and contribution process. |

No edges between E002, E003, and E004: once the format exists, the Dashboard
